fresh_research.topic: BoE 2025 versus 2026 matched control strengthens expectation-adjusted maturity-composition mechanism
fresh_research.label: SOVEREIGN DURATION / MATCHED POLICY CONTROL / METHOD VALIDATION
observed_facts: In September 2025 the BoE reduced its annual APF rundown target from GBP100B to GBP70B and changed active-sale weights to roughly 40% short, 40% medium and 20% long. The Reuters poll median had expected about GBP67.5B, so the aggregate slowdown was substantially anticipated.

The 2025 same-day market reaction was mild: Reuters-republished market data showed the 2-year gilt yield about 2.5bp lower and the 30-year about 1bp lower, consistent with little special long-end surprise.

Before the September 2026 review, the BoE July Market Participants Survey median expected a GBP50B APF stock reduction for Oct.2026-Sep.2027; among respondents expecting active sales, the mean expected maturity weights were 43.3% short, 41.1% medium and 15.6% long.

The September 2026 decision set a multi-year average rundown of GBP46B per year and GBP20B annual active sales, so the aggregate pace was only modestly below the July survey median. The much larger structural change was the long-end path: GBP120B of the longest APF gilts, including all gilts maturing after 2049 and part of the 2049 issue, were retained to back banknotes; GBP222B of shorter holdings were designated to mature naturally; GBP146B maturing from 2035 to 2049 were designated for future sales; APF auctions were paused while a possible DMO implementation model is reviewed.

After the September 2026 announcement, Reuters reported the 30-year gilt yield fell about 12bp to 5.74%, versus about 8bp for the 10-year and 6bp for the 2-year, even though the Bank Rate decision itself remained hawkish: Bank Rate was held at 3.75% and three MPC members voted for a 25bp hike.

BoE July 2026 analysis estimates cumulative QT since 2022 raised 10-year gilt yields by only about 20-30bp, while roughly 200bp of the broader rise in term premia reflected a much wider set of forces including global policy uncertainty, high sovereign issuance and structurally weaker domestic long-duration demand.
fresh_research.inference: The 2025/2026 matched comparison supports, without proving a universal elasticity, the view that sovereign-bond markets respond to the EXPECTATION-ADJUSTED change in market-facing duration by maturity rather than the headline annual QT number. In 2026 the aggregate rundown surprise was small relative to survey expectations, while the long-duration path changed much more materially and the 30-year sector outperformed the front end despite a hawkish short-rate backdrop. In 2025 the largely expected slowdown and maturity skew produced only a mild long-end reaction.
fresh_research.causal_chain: pre-event expected APF runoff/sales by maturity -> realized retention/maturity/sale path differs -> expected private free-float duration at the long end falls relative to prior expectations -> marginal pension/insurer/dealer/relative-value buyers face less price-insensitive supply -> long-term term premium falls relative to front-end policy-rate pricing -> long yields rally even while Bank Rate expectations can remain hawkish
fresh_research.capital_source_destination: The mechanism is principally a change in who must absorb duration and at what yield, not evidence of a cash injection into risk assets. Any spillover into equities, mortgages or credit occurs secondarily through lower long discount rates and financing costs.
fresh_research.matched_control: September 2025: QT slowdown and long-sale skew were broadly expected; 30-year gilt reaction was around -1bp versus roughly -2.5bp for 2-year. September 2026: aggregate pace near survey expectation but a much stronger structural long-duration retention/sales-path change; 30-year about -12bp versus 2-year about -6bp. Concurrent global bond/oil news prevents causal purity, so this is mechanism-supporting rather than a calibrated causal coefficient.
negative_findings: Do not interpret the GBP46B average rundown as the sole causal variable; it was close to the survey median GBP50B expectation.

Do not say all long gilts will never be sold: the retained GBP120B consists of the longest holdings, while the GBP146B sale pool spans 2035-2049 maturities and future implementation is still being designed.
Do not infer a universal basis-point effect from QT dollars or from this single event.
Do not merge the short-rate policy channel with the duration/term-premium channel; the September 2026 event shows they can move in opposite directions.
Do not treat the BoE decision as pure monetary easing: the Bank Rate stance remained hawkish and the balance-sheet plan still removes monetary-policy holdings over time.

learning_candidate.claim: For sovereign bond markets, model expectation-adjusted private/free-float duration equivalents by maturity and marginal-buyer risk-bearing capacity rather than scalar QE/QT or balance-sheet dollars. Separate policy-rate expectations, central-bank holdings/retention/reinvestment/runoff/sales, fiscal issuance, debt-manager operations and buyer capacity.

fresh_research.decision_support: Research-model upgrade only; no standalone sovereign-duration BUY/SHORT is authorized from this mechanism.

fresh_research.topic: Treasury buybacks are liquidity/intermediation operations, not automatic net duration removal
fresh_research.label: U.S. DEBT MANAGEMENT / CAUSAL MODEL CORRECTION
observed_facts: On August 19, 2026 the U.S. Treasury at least doubled the maximum size of long-end liquidity-support buybacks in the 10-20y and 20-30y nominal sectors from $2B to at least $4B per operation, citing strong high-quality offers and a desire to support liquidity.

Treasury's August 3, 2026 borrowing estimate explicitly states that buybacks are not expected to significantly affect privately-held net marketable borrowing because new issuance replaces securities bought back.

Treasury's buyback design materials describe liquidity-support buybacks as an outlet for off-the-run holdings that can free dealer/intermediary balance sheet and improve willingness to make markets. They are not intended as a fixed-quantity QE program or as an acute-stress backstop.

Treasury officials have said the buyback program is small relative to total debt and has changed weighted-average maturity only by a few weeks; direct effects on broad duration are therefore limited unless replacement issuance composition materially differs.

Treasury uses duration-adjusted ten-year-equivalent measures in evaluating auction participation for expanded direct buyback access, reinforcing that notional dollars and duration exposure are distinct state variables.
fresh_research.inference: Gross Treasury buyback volume must not be subtracted mechanically from private duration supply. The correct bridge is buyback security/maturity and dealer-balance-sheet relief minus replacement issuance and its maturity/duration. Buybacks can improve local liquidity and reduce intermediation frictions while leaving net marketable borrowing largely unchanged.
fresh_research.causal_chain: Treasury buys off-the-run securities -> dealers/investors gain a price-sensitive exit and balance-sheet capacity -> local liquidity/on-the-run-off-the-run dislocations can improve -> Treasury replaces financing through issuance -> net private borrowing may be little changed -> duration effect depends on maturity/duration difference between bought-back and replacement securities rather than gross buyback dollars
negative_findings: Do not classify Treasury liquidity-support buybacks as QE.
Do not subtract gross buybacks one-for-one from net Treasury supply.
Do not infer that doubling the operation cap creates a commensurate fall in long yields; actual accepted amounts, replacement issuance, pre-event expectations and market depth matter.
Do not mix market-functioning/liquidity effects with the portfolio-balance duration channel.
fresh_research.method_upgrade_candidate: In the sovereign-duration state vector, track debt-manager buybacks as two legs: securities removed by CUSIP/maturity/duration and replacement issuance by maturity/duration, plus a separate dealer/intermediation-liquidity variable.
